advances: Refutes restricting the sharp mixed-depth selector to the centroid hull. The depth bound is on that candidate set, and the example lies in the three-planar-slice class where the sharp existence theorem applies.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
The hull is a compact rational polytope with interior, since the middle triangle and a point at another base affinely span $\mathbb R^3$. Its base projection is $[-1,1]$. Extremality gives the stated endpoint fibers. At base zero the endpoint coefficients in any grouped convex combination are equal, and their normalized continuous contribution belongs to $((2-s)A+sA)/2=A\subset T$. Thus its whole middle fiber is $T$.

Write $c=|T|=1/2$, $a=|(2-s)A|$, $b=|sA|$, $e=32s^2/125$, and $\delta=128\eta/125$. Then
$$
b/c=e,\qquad (a-b)/c=1-\delta,\qquad W/c=2+2e-\delta.
$$
Indeed $(32/125)((2-s)^2-s^2)=1-\delta$. The bounds $0<\eta<10^{-6}$ and $3/128<s<1/40$ give $9/64000\le e<1/6250$ and $0<\delta<2\cdot10^{-6}$. They give $2e>\delta$ and hence $c<a+b$. Also $W/2-a=c\delta/2=1/4096000$, and $a>b$. All three areas are strictly below $W/2$.

The area centroids of $A,T$ are $g_A=(4/15,8/75)$ and $g_0=(1/3,1/3)$. The only points of $G$ at the endpoint bases are the lifts of $(2-s)g_A$ and $s g_A$. At base zero the same equal-coefficient calculation gives the full segment $[g_A,g_0]$. Its coordinates obey $x+y=(22y+4)/17$.

Put $h=1/3-17e/52$, $k=2/3-11e/26=(22h+4)/17$, and $B=(8/25)(1-s)$. The estimates on $e$ give $8/25<h<1/3$ and $0<k<2/3$. Use the closed ambient halfspaces
$$
H_A=\{y+Bz\ge h\},\qquad H_B=\{x+y-2z\le k\}.
$$
On each endpoint fiber the maximum of $y+Bz$ is $8/25$, so $H_A$ excludes both. Its middle trace has area $c(1-h)^2$. The trace of $H_B$ at $-1$ is empty because its threshold for $x+y$ is $k-2<0$. At $1$ it is the whole fiber because the maximum is $(4/5)s<1/50<k+2$. Its middle trace has area $ck^2$, so its total mass is $c(k^2+e)$. Points of the centroid segment with $y\ge h$ belong to $H_A$ and those with $y\le h$ belong to $H_B$.

The masses of $H_A,H_B$ divided by $c$ are respectively $4/9+(17/39)e+(289/2704)e^2$ and $4/9+(17/39)e+(121/676)e^2$. The second is larger, and the gap after division by $c$ is
$$
(2/9)(W/c)-(k^2+e)=e/117-(256/1125)\eta-(121/676)e^2
>10^{-6}-(4\cdot10^6)^{-1}-10^{-8}>0.
$$
Here $9/(64000\cdot117)>10^{-6}$, $256/1125<1/4$, and $(121/676)/6250^2<10^{-8}$.

For the endpoint centroids use respectively
$$
\{y-2(z+1)\ge (2-s)8/75\},\qquad
\{y+2(z-1)\ge s8/75\}.
$$
All fiber heights in the $y$ coordinate are at most one, so each cap excludes both other fibers. Each contains the corresponding centroid on its boundary and cuts that endpoint triangle by a line parallel to its horizontal edge. The retained similar triangle has linear ratio $2/3$, giving mass $4a/9$ or $4b/9$, strictly below $2W/9$. This accounts for every point of $G$ at an integer base.
statement:
In $\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^2$, let $T=\operatorname{conv}(0,(1,0),(0,1))$, $A=\operatorname{conv}(0,(4/5,0),(0,8/25))$, $\eta=2^{-20}$ and $s=3/128+\eta$. Let $C$ be the convex hull of the lifts of $(2-s)A,T,sA$ at bases $-1,0,1$, respectively. These are precisely its three integer fibers, each with area strictly less than half their total $W$. The larger endpoint fiber has area $W/2-1/4096000$.

Let $G$ be the convex hull of the three lifted area centroids. Every point of $G\cap(\mathbb Z\times\mathbb R^2)$ has raw closed ambient halfspace depth strictly less than $2W/9$.
title: The convex hull of the actual fiber centroids can miss every sharp center
